result.rationale: The diff in EventManager.ts changes `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId` to `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so video-type references now record credentialId: undefined instead of the credential that created the meeting. The loss of stored credentialId on video references is directly visible; the downstream rescheduling impact is plausible but not fully verifiable from this diff alone.

judged_text: EventManager.create now writes credentialId: undefined for video-type booking references, where it previously stored result.credentialId. Bookings that use a dedicated video integration no longer record which credential created the meeting, so flows that resolve the video credential from the booking reference (e.g., reusing the same Zoom credential when rescheduling) find none and fall back to a default credential, creating the rescheduled meeting under the wrong integration account.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, when building booking references, the diff changes `credentialId` for non-calendar (video) integrations from `result.credentialId` to `undefined`: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId` -> `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` (and similarly later `result.credentialId ?? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId` -> `result.credentialId ?? undefined`). This means dedicated video integrations will no longer persist the credentialId in the booking reference, matching the finding’s described regression.
